header: THE LOGIC OF THE DURGAPUR AREAS CARD (pure, no React): here I keep the colour of a PIN code, the facts of the two legislative seats, and the search of the wards and of the post offices. The data is in data.ts (with its sources); how it is drawn is in PincodeCard.tsx. Tested in pincode.selftest.ts.

symbols.name: DURGAPUR_PINS
doc: I take the PIN codes of the 7132xx series (19 exist, 713201 to 713219), then add the two Kanksa codes of the rolls

symbols.name: ALL_PINS
doc: THE COLOUR OF A PIN CODE: I give each of the 21 codes one hue, evenly spaced round the colour wheel (17 degrees apart) and dealt out so that neighbouring codes (713203, 713204) are far apart (8 steps = 137 degrees). The text of the PIN is always shown too: colour is never the only sign.

symbols.name: LIGHTNESS
doc: I also vary the lightness: hues that are neighbours on the wheel (17 degrees apart) differ in lightness too, in three levels taken in turn, so two codes of nearly the same hue still look different

symbols.name: SeatFacts
doc: Describes the two assembly seats (constituencies) of the city, with the numbers of the Delimitation Commission's order

symbols.name: ALIASES
doc: NAMES USED FOR THE SAME PLACE: the roll writes "Ambuja Residential Complex", the people of the city also say "Bengal Ambuja". I make a search by the second find the first. [what people say, what the roll has]

doc: Turns a typed search with the alias names into the names of the roll

symbols.name: NamePiece
doc: I cut an area name into pieces so that the card can write the other name right after the word it belongs to: "Indian Oil Staff Quarters and Ambuja [also Bengal Ambuja] Residential Complex". A piece is plain text, or a word of the roll with its other name. A word that already has the other name in front of it ("Bengal Ambuja") I leave alone.

behaviours: 19 PIN codes exist in the 7132xx series, 713201 to 713219, and none outside
the two Kanksa codes of the rolls are there, outside the series
every PIN has at least one post office with a name, a kind and a block text
713201 has the head office Durgapur, first in its list, and Durgapur RS is the one that does not deliver
the Steel Plant lens: 713203 (Steel Project), 713204 (Steel Town West) and 713205 (Steel Town East) carry a post office named for the plant, and no other PIN of the city does
no two PIN codes have a colour within 15 degrees of each other (21 codes), and consecutive PINs are at least 90 degrees apart
a colour is a set of five hsl() strings and the same PIN always gives the same one
43 wards, 1 to 43, each once
the wards the pages gave for Durgapur Purba are exactly those of the Delimitation Commission's order: 1-10 and 23-28
...and for Durgapur Paschim: 11-22 and 29-43
the seats have the numbers 276 and 277, and sit in the Lok Sabha seat 39 Bardhaman-Durgapur
every polling area of the roll is counted once: 306 for Paschim, 212 for the wards of Purba and 79 for the three gram panchayats (291 in all)
the PIN counts of a ward add up to its polling areas, and every PIN a ward or panchayat uses is a PIN with post offices
every ward has areas, each area has its Bengali (with Bengali letters), its English (Latin letters) and a PIN the ward uses; no area is the roll's '999' line
the three gram panchayats are Amlajora, Gopalpur and Molandighi, as in the order, with 27, 31 and 21 polling areas
the data carries its date
ward 11 (Kuruiya) is PIN 713203 only; ward 29 (Sagarbhanga) is 713211 only; ward 22 has 713216 first (19 areas), then 713209 and 713205
ward 28 has 19 polling areas and PIN 713219 first (part 212 was read by eye)
wardsOfPin: 713211 is only ward 29; 713203 is used by wards 11, 12, 13, 14, 16 and 34 (and no other)
the Kanksa codes belong to the panchayats: 713169 is Amlajora (Shilampur), 713148 is Gopalpur
tokens are lower-case words without punctuation
'ward 22' and 'ward22' are ward 22; a seat, a PIN and a word are told apart
an empty search keeps all 43 wards with all their areas
'ward 22' finds only ward 22; 'purba' finds the 16 wards of the seat; 'paschim' 27
a PIN finds the wards that use it: 713211 is ward 29 only; two PINs at once find the wards that have both
a search for 'Bengal Ambuja' finds exactly what 'Ambuja' finds (the roll writes 'Ambuja Residential Complex')
the other name is written right after the word Ambuja inside the long area name, and nowhere else; one entry in the table
a word finds the wards with that area, in English, and shows only the matching areas
a Bengali word finds the same
words and a ward number together narrow it: 'ward 29 colony' keeps ward 29 only
nothing found gives nothing
PIN search: all 19 for nothing; '713203' finds that one; 'steel project' finds 713203 with that office only; 'steel town' finds 713204 and 713205
searchAreas filters a list by words, English or Bengali, and returns it whole for none
areas grouped by PIN come in the order of the ward's PINs (the biggest first) and lose none
rangesText joins runs
the four stations share the 597 roll parts: Durgapur 325, Coke Oven 111, Kanksa 81, New Township 80
every ward's and panchayat's stations add up to its roll parts, and every area carries a station that the ward has
the gram panchayats of Kanksa are 79 parts of Kanksa station and one of Coke Oven (part 212 is Sagarbhanga, ward 28)
a few known wards: ward 1 is wholly Durgapur station; ward 23 wholly New Township; ward 29 wholly Coke Oven; ward 28 has New Township, Coke Oven and Kanksa
places under a station: Coke Oven covers wards in number order, with only its own areas; Kanksa covers two wards' parts and the three gram panchayats
the station of an area is found by its name: 'Bengal Ambuja' is under the same station as 'Ambuja', and only that station lists it
an empty search lists every area once, under its one station; 'ward 22' lists only that ward; nothing matching gives nothing
the stations' facts: four, with addresses and pages on the Commissionerate's site and no Bengali; the order is by roll parts

the numbers are in the forms the sources publish: a Durgapur landline 0343-xxxxxxx where there is one, the Commissionerate's mobile 91478894xx, an office number 0343-2999xxx; Kanksa has no landline; every station says whom it reports to

the posts: Durgapur PS has five investigation centres (B-Zone, City Centre, Faridpur, Waria, DTPS), New Township PS the Bidhannagar outpost, Coke Oven and Kanksa none; each has a source, a landline in the Durgapur form, and an address
the posts whose station the sources do not state (A-Zone, Banbahal) are kept apart and are under no station; the one near the Steel Plant's gate is Waria, under Durgapur PS

the search of posts: 'waria' finds Waria under Durgapur PS, 'bengal ambuja' and 'ambuja' the City Centre centre, 'bidhannagar' the outpost under New Township PS; a ward, a PIN or only the words police station find none

the two other stations of the subdivision (Women PS and Faridpur PS) have an address, the Commissionerate's mobile and their page; the emergency number is 112; the four sources are named with their address and what to know of each
